title: AI assistants
seoTitle: AI Assistants & Business System Integration | EFIops
metaDescription: Connect AI assistants to business knowledge, records and defined workflows. Scope a practical text or voice assistant with clear limits and human handover.
h1: Ask a question. Get somewhere useful.
eyebrow: AI assistants · Connected to the work
lead: “When will this order arrive?” “Where is that procedure?” Give your team a more direct route to authorised information, with useful source references and a person to help when the answer needs a closer look.

sections.heading: The useful answer often lives behind another screen.
paragraphs: Someone needs a stock location, a job update, a procedure or the next person to contact. The information exists, but finding it means switching tools, asking colleagues or waiting for a reply.
An assistant can provide a more convenient starting point when its knowledge, permissions and actions are carefully defined.

sections.heading: Start with a task worth making easier.
items: Business-data assistants. Retrieve approved records through defined queries and APIs.
Knowledge assistants. Help people find relevant procedures and documents, with references where the source supports them.
Request routing. Collect the required details and send a request into the appropriate workflow or queue.
Text and voice interfaces. Explore an interface inside an existing application, or a focused voice pilot.
Human review dashboards. Show unresolved requests, conversation summaries and work that needs attention.

sections.heading: Clear access. Defined actions. A visible handover.
paragraphs: We agree the assistant's job, identify the sources it may use and define the actions it may request. Access checks and workflow rules stay in the application. Important actions can require review, and uncertain requests can be handed to a person with the relevant context.
A pilot is tested on representative questions, incomplete requests and cases outside its scope. That establishes what works before the assistant is expanded.

faqs.question: Can an assistant use our SQL data?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a suitable integration. The application should expose authorised lookups rather than give a model unrestricted database access.

faqs.question: Can it work inside an application we already have?
faqs.answer: That is often the best starting point. We review the application's architecture and available APIs before choosing the integration.

faqs.question: Can it make changes as well as answer questions?
faqs.answer: Potentially. Each action needs a defined scope, permission checks and an appropriate confirmation or review step.

faqs.question: Can you build an AI phone assistant?
faqs.answer: A scoped phone or voice pilot is a possible project. Call handling, provider costs, consent requirements and human escalation need to be agreed before it becomes a live service.

cta.text: Tell us what people ask, where the answer lives and what should happen after the conversation.

primaryIntent: AI business assistant development; AI integration into existing systems.
summary: Find information and start defined workflows through a connected text or voice assistant.

useCases.title: Where is order 1042?
useCases.body: Retrieve the authorised order record and delivery status. Pass a missing or conflicting answer to a person with the context attached.

useCases.title: Which procedure should I use?
useCases.body: Find the relevant approved document and point back to the source, rather than asking colleagues to remember every detail.

useCases.title: Can I ask instead of opening five screens?
useCases.body: Explore a focused text or voice interface for a read-only lookup or a controlled request inside your existing application.

journey.heading: From a customer question to an answer with a source.
journey.example: A support team wants delivery answers from authorised order records.
journey.question: Can we answer this—or should a person help?
scope: Route unsupported changes to a person
journey.boundary: Payment decisions and unapproved record changes are outside the assistant’s role.

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Start with the questions people actually ask.
stages.body: We review recurring support questions, the information needed to answer them and the requests that need a person. We inspect where the records live and how access is controlled.
stages.output: A question set, source inventory and boundaries for the assistant.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Agree what the assistant may answer or do.
stages.body: The first pilot reads delivery status from authorised order records. It shows the source and asks for help when information is missing. We agree data access, provider dependencies and the escalation route.
stages.output: A focused pilot scope and clear answer/action limits.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Connect the conversation to useful information.
stages.body: You review the answer alongside its source record. We refine the wording, missing-information prompts and handoff so the assistant fits the team’s actual support process.
stages.output: A reviewable assistant connected to the agreed sources.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Test useful answers and sensible limits.
stages.body: Representative questions include delivery updates, missing orders and address changes. We check that the assistant uses the right record, respects access and does not fill an information gap with a confident guess.
stages.output: An evaluation set, documented limitations and an escalation path.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Give the team a way to keep answers current.
stages.body: The handover explains source ownership, provider configuration and how to review poor answers. New knowledge or actions need a controlled update and another round of relevant checks.
stages.output: A source-maintenance guide and a review process for assistant behaviour.

tests.label: Delivery update
tests.reason: The response uses the authorised record, not an invented tracking update.

tests.label: Change address
tests.reason: A request to change data needs a separate authorised action.

tests.label: Order not found
tests.reason: Do not invent an order or expose another customer’s details.

handover.title: Sources & permissions
handover.body: The records and guidance the assistant can access, and who keeps them current.

handover.title: Limits & escalation
handover.body: Unsupported requests, missing information and the handoff to the support team.

handover.title: Review & improvement
handover.body: A question set, evaluation approach and a way to report answers that need attention.
